Result of `render.screenshot`.

data.description:
The image bytes as standard (RFC 4648) base64 of the PNG. The command path favours a
self-contained JSON payload over the binary frame channel; agents decode this directly.

format.description: The image encoding — always `"png"` in M1.

stale.description:
Whether this image's global illumination was *held* rather than rebuilt for the world it
shows (`render.gi_rebake` at `hold`). An agent that screenshots a stale world learns so
from the same reply, instead of reasoning about light that is one edit out of date.

oneOf.description: Result of `render.dump_graph` — the render graph structure as JSON.

graph.description: The graph description (opaque to this crate; produced by `ludion-render-graph`).

oneOf.description: Result of `render.dump_timings` — per-pass GPU timings as JSON.

timings.description: The timings document (opaque to this crate).

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.bounds` — the world AABB and screen rect of every renderable entity under
the current camera (pure CPU; no GPU). Entities are in the same ascending-slot order `extract`
walks, so the response is a deterministic function of the world.

entities.description: One entry per renderable entity (sprite, billboard, mesh, or text), in extract order.

render_size.description: The pixel resolution the screen rects are expressed in (the engine's render size).

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.gi_rebake` — the lever's setting after the command applied, and the
staleness of the last frame this host produced. Every form of the command answers with both,
so a client that only wants to *read* sends empty params.

mode.description: The rebake lever, after any `mode` in the request was applied.

stale.description:
Whether the last frame this host produced showed held global illumination. A requested
rebake has not run yet when this reply is written, so it still describes the frame
before it.

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.size` — the extent in force once the command applied. Every form of the
command answers with it, so a client that only wants to *read* sends empty params, and one
that set an extent learns the resulting pair rather than assuming its request was taken
verbatim.

height.description: The session's render height in pixels. See `width`.

width.description:
The session's render width in pixels: what live stream frames are produced at, and what a
dimensionless `render.screenshot` defaults to.

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.view` — the view override in force once the command applied, or `null`
when the stream is back on the scene's own `Camera`. Every form of the command answers with
it, so a client that only wants to *read* sends empty params.

pose.description: The pose the stream is flying at, or `None` for the scene camera.

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.debug` — the debug-draw categories enabled once the command applied, and
the categories the last completed tick emitted lines for. Every form of the command answers
with both, so a client that only wants to *read* sends empty params.

drawn.description:
The categories the last completed tick emitted lines for, sorted, whether or not they are
enabled — so enabling a category nobody draws shows up as a missing entry here.

view.description:
The SSR debug view in force. It does not say whether the view was drawn: a view on a
frame without SSR draws the normal frame, and `render.dump_graph` shows whether
`ssr_debug` is scheduled.

oneOf.description: Result of `stream.subscribe`.

sub.description: The new subscription id; events on the channel carry it as their `sub`.

oneOf.description: Result of `asset.reload`.

paths.description: The asset paths that were reloaded.

oneOf.description: Result of `engine.describe` — the full machine-readable engine surface.

description.description: Component schemas from the registry plus the protocol schema (opaque to this crate).

oneOf.description: Result of `engine.snapshot` — the serialized engine state.

snapshot.description: The snapshot document; feed it back to `engine.restore` (opaque to this crate).

oneOf.description:
Result of `engine.restore` — the migration report (empty = a clean, lossless restore).

Restore is a migration, not a strict round-trip: component-schema drift between the snapshot
and the running build is reported here (dropped and field-migrated components) rather than
failing the restore. See [`RestoreReport`](crate::restore::RestoreReport).

report.description: What the migration had to change to load the snapshot (empty when nothing changed).

oneOf.description:
Result of `profile.capture` — one performance report over the measured live frames.

The same shape the offline `ludion profile` driver writes (see [`perf`](crate::perf)), so a
budget file, a chart, or a trace exporter reads either source unchanged.

report.description: The measured window, reshaped as a report.

RestoreEntry.description:
One change an `engine.restore` migration made to a single component of a single entity.

The two `Component…` drop variants map to diagnostic codes ([`code`](RestoreEntry::code)); the
informational [`ComponentMigrated`](RestoreEntry::ComponentMigrated) field-diff has none. Run
`ludion explain L3015` / `L3016` for the full explanation of each drop.

oneOf.description:
The snapshot named a component this build no longer registers, so it was **dropped** — the
entity restored without it. Diagnostic code `L3015`.

component.description: The dropped component's registry name (as stored in the snapshot).

entity.description: The entity the dropped component belonged to.

oneOf.description:
The component is still registered, but its snapshotted value no longer deserializes into the
current type, so it was **dropped** — the entity restored without it. Diagnostic code `L3016`.

entity.description: The entity the dropped component belonged to.

error.description: The serde failure text explaining why the value would not deserialize.

oneOf.description:
The component was **kept**, but its serialized shape changed: `filled` field names came from
serde defaults (added to the type since the snapshot), and `removed` field names were present
in the snapshot but no longer exist on the type. Every other field restored verbatim. This is
informational — no diagnostic code — and is only reported when at least one field changed.

entity.description: The entity whose component was migrated.

filled.description:
Field paths newly filled from serde defaults (added since the snapshot), sorted; a nested
field is dotted (`inner.b`).

removed.description:
Field paths present in the snapshot but no longer on the type (dropped), sorted; a nested
field is dotted.

oneOf.description:
The snapshot was captured by a different engine version than this build. The restore went
ahead; this is a warning, not a refusal. Diagnostic code `L3048`.

snapshot_version.description: The engine version stored in the snapshot.

oneOf.description:
The snapshot document carried a top-level field this build does not define; the restore
ignored it. Diagnostic code `L3049`.

entries.description: One entry per divergence the migration found (empty = clean restore).

ScreenRect.description: A screen-space rectangle in pixels, origin top-left, `x`/`y` at the top-left corner.

x.description: Left edge in pixels (may be negative when the entity extends off the left of the viewport).

y.description: Top edge in pixels (may be negative when the entity extends off the top of the viewport).

SeveritySchema.description:
Mirrors [`ludion_core::diagnostics::Severity`]'s serde form: the lowercase strings `"error"`
and `"warning"`.

SimProfile.description:
Sim-side timings — the schedule's per-system medians, the sequential per-tick costs, and the
frame total.

frame_total_median_ms.description: Median wall time of one full sim frame (the observed schedule run plus per-frame overhead).

frame_total_tail.description:
Worst-frame statistics of the frame total. Filled by the offline driver and a replay
profile; `None` for a live capture and for a report predating the field.

sequential.description:
The tick's **sequential** costs — the per-tick work that is per-*world*, not per-entity, and
so cannot be split across threads. One [`SystemTiming`] each, same median statistic as
`systems`, always present in a fixed order. Measured beside the schedule, never inside it: none
of them is part of `frame_total_median_ms`, so a parallelizable share is
`Σ systems / (frame_total + Σ sequential)` — the Amdahl split. The offline driver reports
three (`world_hash`, `extract`, `command_drain`); a live capture reports the two a streaming
tick actually pays (`extract`, `submit`).

systems.description:
Per-system median wall time, in registration order. Empty when the profiled scene runs no
game systems (a scene loaded through the built-in registry has none — the CLI cannot link a
game's own systems, so its `systems` list is the built-in schedule's, which is empty).

threads.description:
How many `ludion_core::par` workers the measured sim ran on.

Results never depend on this — the sim is bit-identical at any worker count — but every
duration above does, so a report is not comparable to another one taken at a different count.
It varies per machine by design (`LUDION_THREADS`, a host's `--threads`, else the machine's
capped available parallelism), which is exactly why it travels with the measurement instead of
being something a reader has to remember.

`None` only in a report predating the field — historical committed JSON, whose worker count
lives in its filename if anywhere. Any live or offline capture fills it.

SubId.description: A subscription id, minted by the server in the `stream.subscribe` response.

SunCascadeProfile.description:
Sun cascade planning — what the sun asked for and what the frame fitted.

Not measurements: the numbers are the shape of the frame's plan, reduced from the same fit and
per-cascade cull the renderer runs, so two runs of the same frame produce identical numbers.
`count < authored` means the quality capped the cascades; `count` 0 with `authored > 0` means
shadows were masked or the camera was degenerate, so neither the cascades nor the anchored box
drew — the report's `quality.shadows` names the first cause.

authored.description: The cascade count the sun authors; 0 for a sun without `cascades` or a sunless scene.

cascades.description: One entry per fitted cascade, nearest first.

count.description: Cascades fitted this frame; 0 when none ran.

tile_edge.description: Edge of one cascade's shadow tile in texels; 0 when none ran.

casters.description: Instances the cascade's box keeps for the shadow pass.

far.description: View depth, in metres, where the slice ends.

near.description: View depth, in metres, where the slice starts.

SystemTiming.description: One system's median wall time across the measured frames.

tail.description:
The worst-frame statistics beside the median — what a median hides. `None` for a live
capture and for a report predating the field.

TimingTail.description: The tail of one timing's per-frame distribution: the worst frame and the 99th percentile.

max_frame.description:
The produced-frame index (`engine.frame()` after the tick) the maximum occurred at; the
first one if several tie.

max_ms.description: The largest single-frame wall time, in milliseconds.

p99_ms.description: The nearest-rank 99th percentile, in milliseconds: the `ceil(0.99·n)`-th smallest sample.

TransportProfile.description:
Frame-delivery timings — what happens to a rendered frame between the sim thread and the socket.

Filled by the server, which owns both spans: `encode` is the frame's image codec run, `send` is
the write into the connection's sink (queueing for the wire, not the kernel's delivery of it).
There is deliberately no readback segment — the engine's pipelined stream ring folds readback
into its own `submit` span in [`SimProfile::sequential`], where it belongs.

encode_median_ms.description: Median encode time in milliseconds over the window's delivered frames.

encode_ms.description:
Per-frame encode times, aligned to [`ProfileSamples::frames`] (`null` for a frame that was
not delivered). Empty when only medians were recorded.

sampled_frames.description:
How many of the window's frames were delivered, and so timed. Below the window's frame count
whenever a subscriber's latest-wins slot dropped a frame, or nobody was subscribed.

send_median_ms.description: Median sink-write time in milliseconds over the window's delivered frames.

send_ms.description: Per-frame sink-write times, aligned the same way.

ViewPose.description:
A free camera pose for `render.view`: where the view camera stands, where it looks, and how wide
it sees.

Geometry only — the clip planes, and the field of view when this pose omits one, come from the
scene's own `Camera`, so a flown view keeps the game's depth range rather than inventing one.
The override is always a *perspective* camera: an orthographic scene camera contributes its clip
planes and nothing else.

# Example
```
use ludion_protocol::command::ViewPose;

let pose = ViewPose { translation: [0.0, 2.0, 6.0], rotation: [-15.0, 0.0, 0.0], fov_y_deg: None };
assert_eq!(
    serde_json::to_value(&pose).unwrap(),
    serde_json::json!({ "translation": [0.0, 2.0, 6.0], "rotation": [-15.0, 0.0, 0.0] }),
);
```

fov_y_deg.description: Vertical field of view in degrees; omit to keep the scene camera's own.

rotation.description: Orientation as Euler-XYZ **degrees**, the same convention a `Transform`'s rotation carries.

translation.description: World-space position of the view camera.

WireErrorSchema.description:
Mirrors [`ludion_core::diagnostics::Diagnostic`]'s serde form (the wire error object): a
`code`, a `message`, an optional `severity` / `path` / `help`, and any number of `related`
sub-diagnostics.

`severity` is absent on an ordinary error (the core type skips it when it is `Error`), so a
client that ignores the field reads every error exactly as it did before severity existed;
only a lint carries it.

WireHash.description: A 64-bit XXH3 digest as exactly 16 lowercase hex digits.

WorldAabb.description: A world-space axis-aligned bounding box: componentwise `min` ≤ `max`.

rotation.description: World-space rotation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees.

sheared.description:
A rotated child sits under a non-uniform accumulated scale, so the drawn transform has a shear
this translation/rotation/scale cannot express.

anyOf.description: A success: the `ok` payload plus the sim `frame` at which the command applied.

frame.description: The sim frame the command applied at (every mutating success carries it).

game_frame.description:
The gameplay frame at the same boundary: `frame` less every frame the game has held
through its `GameClock`. It is the frame a presentation `started` is stamped with, and
it equals `frame` in a session that never holds.

error.description: The diagnostic explaining the failure (its serde shape is the wire error object).

id.description: The correlation id of the request this answers.

response.title: Response

AssetLoadCounters.description: How many assets of one kind a load decoded or reused.

bytes_read.description: On-disk size of the files those decodes read.

cooked.description: Cooked-store reads (KTX2), counted apart from `decoded`; only `texture` is ever non-zero.

decoded.description: Decode events: one per decoded file, so a map shared by two meshes decodes once.

reused.description: Distinct keys whose first lookup in the window was a cache hit.

ClusterProfile.description:
Clustered-forward light binning — the CPU build's cost, and the occupancy of the tables it built.

The occupancy fields are not measurements: they are the *shape* of the tables, reduced out of the
binning's own counting sort, so two runs of the same frame produce identical numbers and any
change in them is a change in the binning rather than noise. Only `build_median_ms` is a
wall-clock median like the rest of the report.

They travel together because that pairing is the whole point: a `scene`-pass regression with the
occupancy unmoved means per-fragment shading got more expensive, while the same regression *with*
the mean or max list length climbing means the binning got looser. One `ludion profile` run tells
them apart, which a GPU capture previously had to.

build_median_ms.description: Median wall time of one cluster build, in milliseconds, over the measured frames.

lights.description: Lights in the frame's global light array.

max_list_len.description: The longest single cell's list — the worst-case loop a fragment can pay.

mean_list_len.description:
The mean list length **over occupied cells** — the loop length a lit fragment pays where the
loop runs at all. The all-cells mean is `total_refs / cells`, one division away, which is why
this one is the occupied mean rather than a second spelling of a derivable number.

occupied_cells.description:
Cells holding at least one light. The complement is free frame — cells a fragment can read
and pay nothing for.

total_refs.description:
Total index references across every cell. This is the number that grows when conservatism
gets looser, whether or not any single list gets longer.

DecalProfile.description:
Projected decals — the frame's decals by blend mode and what the projector pass plans for them.

Not measurements: the counts are the shape of the frame's plan, reduced from the same packing the
renderer runs, so two runs of the same frame produce identical numbers.

draws.description: Decal draws in the projector pass: runs of consecutive decals sharing a blend and a map.

receiver_meshes.description: Meshes the receiver-id pass redraws; 0 means the pass is not scheduled.

components.description: Its components, keyed by registry name.

entity.description: The destroyed entity's id; the `Parent` values in `components` name ids of this kind.
The entity these bounds belong to.

on_screen.description: Whether `screen_rect` is present and intersects the `[0, render_size]` viewport.

screen_rect.description:
The pixel rect bounding the AABB under the current camera, or `null` when the AABB is entirely
behind the camera.

world_aabb.description: The entity's world-space axis-aligned bounding box.

components.description: The requested component values, keyed by registry name (empty if none were requested).

entity.description: The matched entity.

world.description:
The composed world transform; present only when the query set `world` and the entity has a
`Transform`.

GiRebakeMode.description:
Whether a host's global-illumination caches follow the world or hold the baseline they already
have. The wire form is the bare lowercase name (`"auto"` / `"hold"`).

Host/session state, never world state: it is not hashed into a `WorldHash`, not captured by
`engine.snapshot`, and not recorded into a replay, so a held session simulates and records exactly
as an unheld one does.

# Example
```
use ludion_protocol::command::GiRebakeMode;
assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(GiRebakeMode::Hold).unwrap(), serde_json::json!("hold"));
```

oneOf.description:
Both caches follow the world: a changed input rebuilds. The default, and what every engine
did before the lever existed.

Both caches hold what they have. A key miss serves the retained voxelization and probe
volumes and reports staleness instead of rebuilding — the answer for a live session whose
unmarked movers would otherwise force a full revoxelize plus a full bake every frame.

GpuProfile.description: GPU-side timings — per-pass medians from the frame graph.

available.description:
Whether a GPU adapter was available at all. `false` (with empty `passes`) on a headless host
with no adapter — the sim section is still fully measured. Also `false` for a replay
profile, which measures the sim only.

passes.description: Per-pass median GPU time, in scheduled order.

timestamps_supported.description:
Whether the adapter supports `TIMESTAMP_QUERY`. When `false`, each pass's `median_ms` is
`null` (the shape is stable; the numbers are simply unavailable on that adapter).

LoadProfile.description:
What loading a scene cost — wall time per phase, and deterministic per-kind asset counters.

The phases are **exclusive** self-times: a mesh's map decode counts in `texture_ms`, not
`mesh_ms`, so the phases never overlap. `total_ms` runs from the first phase's start to the end
of the measured load, and `total_ms` minus the sum of the phases is the unattributed share.
The counters are not measurements: two loads of the same scene produce identical numbers, so a
change in them is a change in what gets decoded rather than noise.

assets.description: One entry per asset kind, always all of them, in a fixed order.

docs_ms.description: Time spent walking the content root for data-docs and validating them, on the measured scene load.

first_frame_ms.description: Time to the first rendered frame; absent until the renderer reports it.

gi_bake_ms.description: Time spent baking GI probes; absent until the renderer reports it.

gpu_upload_ms.description:
Time the renderer spent uploading the scene's assets to the GPU; absent until the renderer
reports it.

mesh_ms.description: Time spent decoding mesh documents (their maps count in `texture_ms`).

other_ms.description: Time spent decoding every other asset kind.

probe_bake_ms.description:
Time spent capturing and prefiltering reflection probes the store did not hold; absent when
none was captured.

renderer_init_ms.description: Time spent creating the renderer's device and pipelines; absent until the renderer reports it.

scene_ms.description:
Time spent instantiating the scene document into a world, outside the data-doc walk
and any asset decode.

texture_ms.description: Time spent decoding textures: loose sprite textures and mesh maps alike.

total_ms.description: First phase start to end of the measured load.

voxelize_ms.description: Time spent voxelizing the scene for GI; absent until the renderer reports it.

LocalShadowProfile.description:
Local-light shadow planning — which shadowed lights the frame wanted and which it got.

Not measurements: the counts are the shape of the frame's plan, reduced from the same planner the
renderer runs, so two runs of the same frame produce identical numbers. `skipped > 0` means
opted-in lights the camera sees went unshadowed (the game's `skipped == 0` check). A quality that
masks shadows grants nothing: `granted` is 0, `skipped` equals `requested` and `atlas_edge` is 0,
which is honest for a frame that drew no local shadow — the report's `quality.shadows` names why.

atlas_edge.description: The atlas edge the plan used, in texels; 0 when the quality masks shadows.

granted.description: Lights granted a set of atlas tiles.

requested.description: Casting lights whose footprint touches the camera frustum.

skipped.description: `requested − granted`: candidates that did not fit the caster budget.

views.description: Shadow views drawn: a spot takes one, a point light (or a spot wider than 60°) six.

PassTiming.description: One frame-graph pass's median GPU time across the measured frames.

median_ms.description: Median GPU time in milliseconds, or `null` when the adapter lacks timestamp support.

diagnostic.description:
The `L1234` or `L1230` a save would raise for this instance, in which case the fields above
are empty or false.

name.description: The instance's name, `null` for an unnamed spawn (which a save leaves as plain entities).

overrides.description:
Part path to the JSON pointers of the overridden leaves, each `/<Component>[/<field>...]`.
`/<part path>` followed by a pointer is exactly a `prefab.revert` pointer.

placement_differs.description:
Whether the saved `transform` differs, bit for bit, from the placement the instance was
spawned or loaded at.

prefab.description: The prefab file, relative to the content root.

removed.description: The part paths the instance dropped from its prefab.

root.description: The instance's root, the `PrefabInstance.root` its parts carry; may be a dead entity.

root_parts.description:
The prefab's root part paths, in part order: the parts with no `Parent` in the prefab file.
Their `Transform` and `Parent` are the instance's placement, which `prefab.revert` leaves
alone. Empty when `diagnostic` is set or the prefab cannot be read.

ProbeProfile.description:
The last reflection-probe resolve: probes loaded from the store versus captured.

`hits` stays 0 on the Fresh paths (`ludion profile`, `--profile`), which never read the store, by
design: committed images and measurements never depend on a cache file existing.

hits.description: Probes loaded from the probe store.

ProfileReport.description:
One profiling run's result: the input, the frame counts, and the timing sections.

[`Deserialize`] as well as [`Serialize`]: a report is an artifact tooling reads back — a
committed baseline JSON compared against a later run, an Amdahl split computed off it — not only
something a host prints once. Every optional section defaults to `None`, so a report written
before that section existed still parses; which of them a given report carries depends on which
host produced it, and each field below says so.

cluster.description:
Clustered-forward light binning: what the frame's cluster tables cost to build and how
crowded they came out. Filled by the **offline** driver and absent for a live capture — the
mirror image of `transport`, and for the mirror-image reason: the live host builds its
cluster tables inside a frame a profiler must neither stall nor make pay twice, while the
offline driver owns its own loop and can time the build as its own span.

gpu.description: GPU-side timings: per-pass medians from the render pipeline.

load.description:
What loading the scene cost, phase by phase, and how many assets each kind decoded or reused.
Filled by the **offline** driver and absent for a live capture: a load is a one-off event the
host has already run by the time a capture asks, and a disarmed host reads no clock for it.

local_shadows.description:
Local-light shadow planning: how many shadowed lights the frame requested, was granted and
skipped. Filled by the **offline** driver and absent for a live capture, for `cluster`'s
reason: the live host plans inside a frame a profiler must not make pay twice.

measured_frames.description: Frames measured; every median below is over this many samples.

probes.description:
Reflection probes of the last resolve: loaded from the store versus captured. Absent for a
scene without probes. Filled offline and by a live capture.

quality.description:
The render quality this measurement was taken at — the setting the host chose and the
parameter axes every GPU number below depends on. Filled by the host that owns the setting
(the offline driver directly, the live host when it answers a capture), so `None` means only
a report predating the field.

samples.description: The measured frames' raw per-frame columns, present when the request asked for them.

scene.description:
The scene that was profiled — the path as given on the command line offline, the loaded
scene's name for a live capture.

sim.description: Sim-side timings: per-system medians and the whole-frame median.

sun_cascades.description:
Sun cascade planning: how many cascades the sun authored and the frame fitted, and each
one's depth range, texel size and caster count. Filled by the **offline** driver and absent
for a live capture, for `cluster`'s reason: the live host fits inside a frame a profiler
must not make pay twice.

transport.description:
Frame-delivery timings, filled by the server for a live capture and absent otherwise (the
offline driver delivers no frames, so it has no transport to measure).

warmup_frames.description:
Warmup frames driven and discarded before measuring (JIT/cache settling). Always `0` for a
live capture: the frames it measures are the ones the host was already producing.

ProfileSamples.description:
A window's raw per-frame samples, stored columnar: every name appears once and each measurement
is a parallel array indexed by the window's frame position.

This is what a timeline is drawn from — a median cannot say *when* a spike happened.

extract_ms.description: Per-frame render-scene extraction times (`null` for an unrendered frame).

frames.description: The frame each column entry belongs to, ascending.

pass_ms.description:
One row per entry in [`pass_names`](ProfileSamples::pass_names), each a per-frame array
(`null` where that frame carried no sample, or the adapter cannot time passes).

pass_names.description: GPU pass names, in scheduled order.

submit_ms.description: Per-frame frame-submit times (`null` for an unrendered frame).

system_ms.description: One row per entry in [`system_names`](ProfileSamples::system_names), each a per-frame array.

QualityProfile.description:
The render quality a measurement was taken at: what the machine chose, which optional effects
that resolved to, and how hard each one worked.

It travels with a report for the reason [`SimProfile::threads`] does — two measurements taken
under different machine settings are not comparable, and only the report can say so. Quality is a
per-machine host switch (`--quality`, `LUDION_QUALITY`), never scene content and never sim state,
so nothing here affects a `WorldHash`: a report at `low` and one at `full` describe the same
simulation costing different pixels.

The `preset` label and the six toggles are the *choice*; the parameter axes below them are the
*build* — a shader's sample count or a texture descriptor's size, reported as the renderer
currently runs them. A false toggle leaves that effect's passes out of the frame graph entirely,
so its axis describes work that was not done: `shadows: false` beside a `shadow_map_size` of 1024
means no map of any size was drawn, and reading the axis without the toggle is the misreading
every toggle here exists to prevent.

anti_aliasing.description:
The anti-aliasing mode the frames were drawn with (`off` or `smaa`), as the host resolved it.
SMAA adds three passes after composite, so two reports at different modes are not comparable.

dof.description: Whether depth of field ran on a scene that authored it.

gi_dynamic.description:
Whether per-frame GI dynamic-light injection ran. Masked off, a marked light contributes its
direct lighting only and no injection pass is scheduled.

gi_probe_scale.description:
Multiplier on the scene's authored GI probe spacing; `1.0` bakes at exactly what the scene
asked for.

gi_rays.description: Rays cast per probe by the GI bake.

ibl_specular_size.description: Edge length of a face of the sky's specular cube, in texels.

local_shadow_atlas_size.description:
Edge length of the square local-light shadow atlas, in texels; the caster budget is a fixed
view count, so only resolution follows this.

pcf.description: Edge length of the shadow map's PCF kernel, in taps (`3` is a 3×3 average).

preset.description:
The name of the setting this machine chose: a preset name, or `custom` for a local override
file. Not derivable from the toggles — several presets currently resolve to the same ones.

render_scale.description:
Fraction of the output extent the frame was drawn at before being resampled up to it; `1.0`
is native.

**Every GPU number in this report is a per-pixel cost**, and this is the only field that says
how many pixels they were paid over. A capture at `low` draws 56% of them, so a report naming
its sample counts and its shadow map but not its resolution would show a smaller frame as a
faster one — the same class of lie [`shadows`](QualityProfile::shadows) is here to prevent,
applied to every pass at once rather than to one.

shadow_map_size.description: Edge length of the square sun shadow map, in texels.

shadows.description:
Whether the sun's shadow map was drawn on a scene carrying a sun. Masked off, the `shadow`
pass is not scheduled, the light shafts that march the map go with it, and the sun still
lights the scene.

Not derivable from anything else in this block, which is why it is here: `shafts: false` says
the same thing for a scene that never authored shafts, and an override file reports `custom`
for `preset` — so without this field a capture could report `shadow_map_size` for a frame
that drew no shadow map.

shafts.description: Whether volumetric light shafts ran on a scene that authored them.

ssao.description: Whether ambient occlusion ran on a scene that authored it.

ssr.description:
Whether this machine's quality allows screen-space reflections (a scene still opts in via
`PostProcess.ssr`).

ssr_scale.description: The SSR trace's extent as a fraction of the **output** extent, independent of `render_scale`.

sun_cascades.description:
The most cascades a sun fits on this machine (`min(authored, this)`); a sun without
`cascades` draws the anchored box.

RenderDebugView.description:
A debug view shown in place of the composite: the SSR trace at its own resolution, the probe map,
the local-light shadow atlas, or the lit frame tinted by sun cascade.
The spelling matches `ludion render --debug-view`.

oneOf.description: The per-texel trace confidence as a grey ramp.
The colour-pyramid level each hit read.
The winning reflection probe per pixel, coloured by rank.

The local-light shadow atlas, letterboxed: granted tiles as linearised depth, ungranted cells
dark blue, a red line on every cell border.
Each mesh fragment tinted by the sun cascade that shades it.

RestoreEntry.description:
One change an `engine.restore` migration made to a single component of a single entity.

The two `Component…` drop variants map to diagnostic codes ([`code`](RestoreEntry::code)); the
informational [`ComponentMigrated`](RestoreEntry::ComponentMigrated) field-diff has none. Run
`ludion explain L3015` / `L3016` for the full explanation of each drop.

oneOf.description:
The snapshot named a component this build no longer registers, so it was **dropped** — the
entity restored without it. Diagnostic code `L3015`.

component.description: The dropped component's registry name (as stored in the snapshot).

entity.description: The entity the dropped component belonged to.

oneOf.description:
The component is still registered, but its snapshotted value no longer deserializes into the
current type, so it was **dropped** — the entity restored without it. Diagnostic code `L3016`.

entity.description: The entity the dropped component belonged to.

error.description: The serde failure text explaining why the value would not deserialize.

oneOf.description:
The component was **kept**, but its serialized shape changed: `filled` field names came from
serde defaults (added to the type since the snapshot), and `removed` field names were present
in the snapshot but no longer exist on the type. Every other field restored verbatim. This is
informational — no diagnostic code — and is only reported when at least one field changed.

entity.description: The entity whose component was migrated.

filled.description:
Field paths newly filled from serde defaults (added since the snapshot), sorted; a nested
field is dotted (`inner.b`).

removed.description:
Field paths present in the snapshot but no longer on the type (dropped), sorted; a nested
field is dotted.

oneOf.description:
The snapshot was captured by a different engine version than this build. The restore went
ahead; this is a warning, not a refusal. Diagnostic code `L3048`.

snapshot_version.description: The engine version stored in the snapshot.

oneOf.description:
The snapshot document carried a top-level field this build does not define; the restore
ignored it. Diagnostic code `L3049`.

entries.description: One entry per divergence the migration found (empty = clean restore).

ScreenRect.description: A screen-space rectangle in pixels, origin top-left, `x`/`y` at the top-left corner.

x.description: Left edge in pixels (may be negative when the entity extends off the left of the viewport).

y.description: Top edge in pixels (may be negative when the entity extends off the top of the viewport).

SeveritySchema.description:
Mirrors [`ludion_core::diagnostics::Severity`]'s serde form: the lowercase strings `"error"`
and `"warning"`.

SimProfile.description:
Sim-side timings — the schedule's per-system medians, the sequential per-tick costs, and the
frame total.

frame_total_median_ms.description: Median wall time of one full sim frame (the observed schedule run plus per-frame overhead).

frame_total_tail.description:
Worst-frame statistics of the frame total. Filled by the offline driver and a replay
profile; `None` for a live capture and for a report predating the field.

sequential.description:
The tick's **sequential** costs — the per-tick work that is per-*world*, not per-entity, and
so cannot be split across threads. One [`SystemTiming`] each, same median statistic as
`systems`, always present in a fixed order. Measured beside the schedule, never inside it: none
of them is part of `frame_total_median_ms`, so a parallelizable share is
`Σ systems / (frame_total + Σ sequential)` — the Amdahl split. The offline driver reports
three (`world_hash`, `extract`, `command_drain`); a live capture reports the two a streaming
tick actually pays (`extract`, `submit`).

systems.description:
Per-system median wall time, in registration order. Empty when the profiled scene runs no
game systems (a scene loaded through the built-in registry has none — the CLI cannot link a
game's own systems, so its `systems` list is the built-in schedule's, which is empty).

threads.description:
How many `ludion_core::par` workers the measured sim ran on.

Results never depend on this — the sim is bit-identical at any worker count — but every
duration above does, so a report is not comparable to another one taken at a different count.
It varies per machine by design (`LUDION_THREADS`, a host's `--threads`, else the machine's
capped available parallelism), which is exactly why it travels with the measurement instead of
being something a reader has to remember.

`None` only in a report predating the field — historical committed JSON, whose worker count
lives in its filename if anywhere. Any live or offline capture fills it.

SubId.description: A subscription id, minted by the server in the `stream.subscribe` response.

SunCascadeProfile.description:
Sun cascade planning — what the sun asked for and what the frame fitted.

Not measurements: the numbers are the shape of the frame's plan, reduced from the same fit and
per-cascade cull the renderer runs, so two runs of the same frame produce identical numbers.
`count < authored` means the quality capped the cascades; `count` 0 with `authored > 0` means
shadows were masked or the camera was degenerate, so neither the cascades nor the anchored box
drew — the report's `quality.shadows` names the first cause.

authored.description: The cascade count the sun authors; 0 for a sun without `cascades` or a sunless scene.

cascades.description: One entry per fitted cascade, nearest first.

count.description: Cascades fitted this frame; 0 when none ran.

tile_edge.description: Edge of one cascade's shadow tile in texels; 0 when none ran.

casters.description: Instances the cascade's box keeps for the shadow pass.

far.description: View depth, in metres, where the slice ends.

near.description: View depth, in metres, where the slice starts.

SystemTiming.description: One system's median wall time across the measured frames.

tail.description:
The worst-frame statistics beside the median — what a median hides. `None` for a live
capture and for a report predating the field.

TimingTail.description: The tail of one timing's per-frame distribution: the worst frame and the 99th percentile.

max_frame.description:
The produced-frame index (`engine.frame()` after the tick) the maximum occurred at; the
first one if several tie.

max_ms.description: The largest single-frame wall time, in milliseconds.

p99_ms.description: The nearest-rank 99th percentile, in milliseconds: the `ceil(0.99·n)`-th smallest sample.

TransportProfile.description:
Frame-delivery timings — what happens to a rendered frame between the sim thread and the socket.

Filled by the server, which owns both spans: `encode` is the frame's image codec run, `send` is
the write into the connection's sink (queueing for the wire, not the kernel's delivery of it).
There is deliberately no readback segment — the engine's pipelined stream ring folds readback
into its own `submit` span in [`SimProfile::sequential`], where it belongs.

encode_median_ms.description: Median encode time in milliseconds over the window's delivered frames.

encode_ms.description:
Per-frame encode times, aligned to [`ProfileSamples::frames`] (`null` for a frame that was
not delivered). Empty when only medians were recorded.

sampled_frames.description:
How many of the window's frames were delivered, and so timed. Below the window's frame count
whenever a subscriber's latest-wins slot dropped a frame, or nobody was subscribed.

send_median_ms.description: Median sink-write time in milliseconds over the window's delivered frames.

send_ms.description: Per-frame sink-write times, aligned the same way.

ViewPose.description:
A free camera pose for `render.view`: where the view camera stands, where it looks, and how wide
it sees.

Geometry only — the clip planes, and the field of view when this pose omits one, come from the
scene's own `Camera`, so a flown view keeps the game's depth range rather than inventing one.
The override is always a *perspective* camera: an orthographic scene camera contributes its clip
planes and nothing else.

# Example
```
use ludion_protocol::command::ViewPose;

let pose = ViewPose { translation: [0.0, 2.0, 6.0], rotation: [-15.0, 0.0, 0.0], fov_y_deg: None };
assert_eq!(
    serde_json::to_value(&pose).unwrap(),
    serde_json::json!({ "translation": [0.0, 2.0, 6.0], "rotation": [-15.0, 0.0, 0.0] }),
);
```

fov_y_deg.description: Vertical field of view in degrees; omit to keep the scene camera's own.

rotation.description: Orientation as Euler-XYZ **degrees**, the same convention a `Transform`'s rotation carries.

translation.description: World-space position of the view camera.

WireErrorSchema.description:
Mirrors [`ludion_core::diagnostics::Diagnostic`]'s serde form (the wire error object): a
`code`, a `message`, an optional `severity` / `path` / `help`, and any number of `related`
sub-diagnostics.

`severity` is absent on an ordinary error (the core type skips it when it is `Error`), so a
client that ignores the field reads every error exactly as it did before severity existed;
only a lint carries it.

WireHash.description: A 64-bit XXH3 digest as exactly 16 lowercase hex digits.

WorldAabb.description: A world-space axis-aligned bounding box: componentwise `min` ≤ `max`.

rotation.description: World-space rotation as XYZ Euler angles in degrees.

sheared.description:
A rotated child sits under a non-uniform accumulated scale, so the drawn transform has a shear
this translation/rotation/scale cannot express.

oneOf.description:
A bare acknowledgement — the command succeeded and has no data to return (its effect is
captured by the envelope `frame`). Used by `sim.pause`, `sim.resume`, `sim.set_speed`,
`input.inject`, and `stream.unsubscribe`.
Result of `scene.load`.

entity_count.description: How many entities the loaded scene instantiated.

oneOf.description: Result of `scene.save`.

path.description: The path the canonical YAML was written to.

oneOf.description: Result of `scene.check`.

valid.description: Whether the scene validated with no errors.

oneOf.description: Result of `entity.spawn`.

entity.description: The id of the newly created entity.

oneOf.description:
Result of `entity.destroy` — the destroyed entity's full component state at the moment it was
despawned (the undo inverse: `entity.spawn` with these components respawns it, under a fresh
id). Keyed by registry name, sorted by name (`BTreeMap` order); includes `Name` if the entity
carried one — it is a component like any other on the wire. Destroying an entity destroys its
descendants too: `descendants` lists each, every parent before its children, so a client
respawns the root and then each descendant in order, remapping the old ids its `Parent`
components name to the fresh ones.

components.description: The destroyed entity's components, keyed by registry name.

descendants.description: The cascaded descendants, parents before children; empty when the entity had none.

oneOf.description:
Result of `entity.reparent` — the entity's `Parent` and `Transform` immediately before (the
undo inverse: `entity.reparent` with `parent: previous_parent` and `keep: local`, then
`component.set Transform` with `previous_transform` when it is present).

previous_parent.description: The parent the entity had, or `null` for a root.

previous_transform.description: The entity's `Transform` before the call, or `null` when it had none.

oneOf.description:
Result of `prefab.spawn` — the spawned entities in the prefab's part order; the first is the
instance root (`PrefabInstance.root`). The undo is `entity.destroy` on each root part.

entities.description: The new entity ids, one per prefab part, in part order.

oneOf.description: Result of `prefab.create` — the file written.

path.description: The prefab's normalized path, relative to the content root.

oneOf.description: Result of `prefab.apply` — what was written into the prefab file.

parts.description: The part paths whose component overrides were written into the prefab.

path.description: The prefab file written, relative to the content root.

removed.description: The part paths deleted from the prefab.

oneOf.description: Result of `prefab.revert` — what the revert changed.

entities.description: The parts with at least one component written or removed, in live order.

not_restored.description: The prefab's part paths with no live part: removed from the instance, and not re-spawned.

oneOf.description: Result of `prefab.unpack` — the instance's parts, now plain entities.

entities.description: The parts' ids, in live order.

oneOf.description:
Result of `prefab.overrides` — one entry per instance, in request order (all live instances
in world order when none were named).

instances.description: What `scene.save` would write for each instance.

oneOf.description:
Result of `component.set` — the component's value immediately before the set (the undo
inverse: `component.set` with this value restores it), or `None` when the set was a fresh
insert (the entity did not carry the component before).

previous.description: The value the component held immediately before this set, or `None` for a fresh insert.

oneOf.description: Result of `component.get`.

Result of `component.remove` — the removed component's value (the undo inverse:
`component.set` with this value re-inserts it).

previous.description: The value the component held immediately before removal.

oneOf.description: Result of `query.entities`.

entities.description: The matched entities and their requested component values.

oneOf.description: Result of `sim.step`.

hash.description: The `WorldHash` of the resulting state, present iff the request set `hash: true`.

oneOf.description: Result of `sim.hash`.
Result of `render.screenshot`.

data.description:
The image bytes as standard (RFC 4648) base64 of the PNG. The command path favours a
self-contained JSON payload over the binary frame channel; agents decode this directly.

format.description: The image encoding — always `"png"` in M1.

stale.description:
Whether this image's global illumination was *held* rather than rebuilt for the world it
shows (`render.gi_rebake` at `hold`). An agent that screenshots a stale world learns so
from the same reply, instead of reasoning about light that is one edit out of date.

oneOf.description: Result of `render.dump_graph` — the render graph structure as JSON.

graph.description: The graph description (opaque to this crate; produced by `ludion-render-graph`).

oneOf.description: Result of `render.dump_timings` — per-pass GPU timings as JSON.

timings.description: The timings document (opaque to this crate).

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.bounds` — the world AABB and screen rect of every renderable entity under
the current camera (pure CPU; no GPU). Entities are in the same ascending-slot order `extract`
walks, so the response is a deterministic function of the world.

entities.description: One entry per renderable entity (sprite, billboard, mesh, or text), in extract order.

render_size.description: The pixel resolution the screen rects are expressed in (the engine's render size).

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.gi_rebake` — the lever's setting after the command applied, and the
staleness of the last frame this host produced. Every form of the command answers with both,
so a client that only wants to *read* sends empty params.

mode.description: The rebake lever, after any `mode` in the request was applied.

stale.description:
Whether the last frame this host produced showed held global illumination. A requested
rebake has not run yet when this reply is written, so it still describes the frame
before it.

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.size` — the extent in force once the command applied. Every form of the
command answers with it, so a client that only wants to *read* sends empty params, and one
that set an extent learns the resulting pair rather than assuming its request was taken
verbatim.

height.description: The session's render height in pixels. See `width`.

width.description:
The session's render width in pixels: what live stream frames are produced at, and what a
dimensionless `render.screenshot` defaults to.

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.view` — the view override in force once the command applied, or `null`
when the stream is back on the scene's own `Camera`. Every form of the command answers with
it, so a client that only wants to *read* sends empty params.

pose.description: The pose the stream is flying at, or `None` for the scene camera.

oneOf.description:
Result of `render.debug` — the debug-draw categories enabled once the command applied, and
the categories the last completed tick emitted lines for. Every form of the command answers
with both, so a client that only wants to *read* sends empty params.

drawn.description:
The categories the last completed tick emitted lines for, sorted, whether or not they are
enabled — so enabling a category nobody draws shows up as a missing entry here.

view.description:
The SSR debug view in force. It does not say whether the view was drawn: a view on a
frame without SSR draws the normal frame, and `render.dump_graph` shows whether
`ssr_debug` is scheduled.

oneOf.description: Result of `stream.subscribe`.

sub.description: The new subscription id; events on the channel carry it as their `sub`.

oneOf.description: Result of `asset.reload`.

paths.description: The asset paths that were reloaded.

oneOf.description: Result of `engine.describe` — the full machine-readable engine surface.

description.description: Component schemas from the registry plus the protocol schema (opaque to this crate).

oneOf.description: Result of `engine.snapshot` — the serialized engine state.

snapshot.description: The snapshot document; feed it back to `engine.restore` (opaque to this crate).

oneOf.description:

Restore is a migration, not a strict round-trip: component-schema drift between the snapshot
and the running build is reported here (dropped and field-migrated components) rather than
failing the restore. See [`RestoreReport`](crate::restore::RestoreReport).

report.description: What the migration had to change to load the snapshot (empty when nothing changed).

oneOf.description:
Result of `profile.capture` — one performance report over the measured live frames.

The same shape the offline `ludion profile` driver writes (see [`perf`](crate::perf)), so a
budget file, a chart, or a trace exporter reads either source unchanged.
